claims.text: In-situ high-temperature TEM combined with EDS mapping can reveal elemental redistribution within nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
Nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution contributes to the formation of protective oxide layers.
The additively manufactured alloy forms more protective oxide layers than conventionally processed counterparts.
Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 can be produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy contains dual nanoprecipitates.
The nanoprecipitates are homogeneously distributed in the initial alloy.
Thin TEM specimens will be oxidized at high temperature while concurrent TEM imaging and EDS mapping are performed.
A controlled oxygen-rich atmosphere in an in-situ TEM holder can mimic relevant gas-turbine or aerospace oxidation conditions.
Nanoprecipitates mediate elemental diffusion during oxidation.
Nanoprecipitates mediate local phase transformations during oxidation.
Elevated temperature promotes redistribution of alloying elements within the nanoprecipitates.
Elemental redistribution drives nucleation and growth of protective oxide phases at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
Oxide phases will emerge from nanoprecipitate sites after measurable elemental shifts occur.
The observed redistribution and site-specific oxide formation will correlate with improved oxidation resistance relative to cast or wrought samples.
Nanoprecipitate redistribution during oxidation is less dynamic in conventionally cast or wrought samples.
Conventionally cast or wrought samples have lower oxidation resistance than the additively manufactured alloy.
The redistribution behavior depends on oxidation temperature, oxygen partial pressure, and nanoprecipitate phase stability.
Sequential EDS maps can quantify time-dependent elemental-concentration changes in nanoprecipitates and the surrounding matrix.
